rationale: The Adobe-C++ functionobjects benchmark is template-heavy C++ with abundant virtual dispatch, STL usage, and small hot function objects, but the profile lacks source-level detail, so the table favors low-risk, broadly applicable transforms over aggressive ones. SUB gets the highest weights across all dimensions because instruction substitution is cheap in both size and runtime, carries near-zero correctness risk, and stacks well with every other pass. FLA and BCF are kept moderately strong (SecurityGain 0.7-0.8) since flattening and bogus control flow are the main reverse-engineering deterrents, but their RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights are lowered (0.3-0.4) because the benchmark's tight, repeatedly invoked function objects amplify loop-level overhead and code bloat. SPLIT is enabled with balanced weights as a low-cost enabler that improves FLA/BCF effectiveness by fragmenting basic blocks. IBR is moderate: the code already contains heavy indirect branching from virtual calls, so added value is real but incremental, with a cautious CorrectnessRisk weight. ICALL and IGV are weighted lowest and their CorrectnessRisk weights are suppressed (0.3-0.4) because C++ vtables, virtual dispatch, and static initialization make indirect-call/global-variable rewriting the passes most likely to break template-instantiated or runtime-initialized constructs, and the program already exhibits plentiful indirect calls, limiting marginal diversity gain.
